title: green-is-earned-not-assumed
intention: Red is the default; green is earned — Law 9 as derived physics, not prose a reader must remember to apply.
why: Akien, 2026-08-04: 'everything not working is red should have been one of the very first rules of our development. so i am so ruling now' + 'a newly minted IDEA is red until it's in code and running.' As prose it binds only the reader who remembers it, at the moment they remember it — which is exactly how a component came to sit for weeks describing a design its code did not implement. The lived symptom: a person reads a charter, believes the component works as described, builds on it, and discovers otherwise later.
traces_to: CP6 — 'The world is not a safe place. We have to build and care for safety as we go.' Ruled 2026-08-04 (2026-08-04-red-is-cp6-and-correction-needs-no-justification): Law 9 is CP6 turned on the corpus, not a new value. That matters to the BUILD, not just the filing — CP6's own falsifier language is the model to copy ('any drift between the code and this record is a red — physics, not a keep-in-sync comment'), and CP6 is already structurally present in every device and shim via CoreValuesMixin, which is the nearest existing carrier for a per-component green.

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a component whose code stops matching its charter, or whose proof goes red, or which has never run, READS as red without anyone marking it — measured by breaking one deliberately and observing the change. AND when the surface can show a lot that has never been broken ground on, because a site plan that only knows about buildings already started is not a site plan. AND when a dependency change produces yellow (not red) in dependents, and self-cleaning via operational logs produces green without human intervention. WRONG INTENT if the answer turns out to be a field somebody sets; if the thing built reports on what EXISTS only — that reads green-by-omission, which is the precise failure the whole-site-starts-red framing is aimed at; or if every dependency change cascades red through the full chain.

how: Derive red/green from built + running + inspected, not from assumption. Build the derivation as a predicate over each component's charter, state, and proofs. No triage authority — everything starts red.
